iut_type: End Product (Alps Alpine HM2-series device), adding a new HID11/CTKD profile to an existing registration -- post-2024 system requires testing the full combined profile set, not just the new profile
customer_question: If we add a new profile (HID11) by referencing an existing Base QDID via a Profile Subsystem registration, do we only need to test HID11 plus the IOPT cases specifically related to HID11? Or does the existing QDID's other profiles' related IOPT cases need testing too?
question_variants: Does this scope expansion only happen when referencing an existing QDID, or also when registering a brand-new Host Subsystem QDID?
Under the old (pre-2024) system, would this have worked differently?
actual_issue: The customer expected that adding a new profile (HID11) to an existing registration via a Profile Subsystem reference would only require testing that new profile plus its directly-related IOPT cases -- consistent with how this worked under the registration system in effect before July 2024 -- but the current system's structural change meant a much larger combined test scope was actually required.
plain_english_explanation: Under the registration rules in effect through June 30, 2024 (PRDv2.3, via the Launch Studio site), the customer's expectation was correct: a 'new Profile Subsystem registration plus an existing DN/QDID reference' was a distinct registration method that only required testing the newly-added profile and its directly-related IOPT cases. However, effective July 1, 2024, the current registration rules (QPRDv3/v4, via the Qualification Workspace site) eliminated that registration method entirely -- it no longer exists as an option. Instead, when referencing (Including) an existing DN/QDID, the full combined set of profiles -- everything the referenced QDID already includes, plus the newly-added profile -- becomes the IOPT test scope as a whole, with the new profile's own ICS-linked test items also required on top of that combined IOPT scope. In this specific case, referencing the existing QDID brought along a substantial inherited profile set (SR/COD, A2DP, AVRCP, DID, DIS, HFP, DUN, MAP, OPP, PAN, PBAP, SPP), each contributing its own IOPT test items, resulting in 22 total IOPT test items required in addition to the HID11-specific PTS test items the customer had already planned for.
consultant_answer: Under the older registration rules (through June 30, 2024, via Launch Studio), your expectation would have been correct -- only the new profile and its directly-related IOPT cases. But the current rules (since July 1, 2024, via Qualification Workspace) eliminated that registration method entirely: referencing an existing QDID now means the full combined profile set -- everything that QDID already includes, plus your newly-added HID11 profile -- becomes the IOPT test scope together, with HID11's own ICS-linked test items required on top. In your case, the existing QDID's inherited profiles bring 22 additional IOPT test items beyond the HID11-specific PTS tests you already planned for.
decision_logic: When a customer plans to add a new profile to an existing registration by referencing (Including) an existing QDID under the current (post-July-2024) registration system, the full IOPT test scope must include every profile the referenced QDID already covers, not just the newly-added profile -- this represents a structural change from the prior registration system, and customers familiar with the old system's lighter scoping rule need this explicitly flagged before they commit to a test plan based on outdated assumptions.
final_recommendation: When a customer proposes adding a new profile via an existing QDID reference, proactively check what profiles that QDID already includes and calculate the full combined IOPT scope before the customer commits to a test plan, rather than letting them discover the expanded scope only after building a test plan based on the older, narrower rule.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer building a test plan based on the outdated, narrower scoping rule would discover only after testing began that a much larger IOPT test scope was actually required, wasting time and potentially requiring a complete test plan redo.
